2KI-003.alt: Hilkiah and Shaphan respectfully hold the discovered scroll in a stone and timber Temple room, writing hidden.
2KI-003.note: The written side and some priestly clothing are hidden. The ancillary room is reconstructed, not a recovered plan.

EZR-001.title: The Temple Foundation Is Laid
EZR-001.q: could not discern the noise of the shout of joy from the noise of the weeping of the people
EZR-001.alt: Priests and Levites celebrate the temple foundation while older witnesses weep among the rejoicing crowd.
EZR-001.note: Silver trumpets are retained after Ezra 3 and Numbers 10; ram horns are not a universal replacement for biblical metal trumpets.

NEH-001.title: Jerusalem’s Wall Rebuilt
NEH-001.q: So the wall was finished in the twenty and fifth day of the month Elul, in fifty and two days.
NEH-001.alt: Nehemiah and workers stand beside the completed wall and an open unfinished gateway of Persian-period Jerusalem.
NEH-001.note: Selected moment with wall complete and gateway doors still pending, informed by Nehemiah 6:1 and 7:1; this does not certify an excavated wall course.

EST-001.title: Esther Before the King
EST-001.q: the king held out to Esther the golden sceptre that was in his hand.
EST-001.alt: Esther approaches with dignity as King Ahasuerus extends his golden scepter within a Persian royal court.
EST-001.note: Esther approaches the offered sceptre before touching it. Persian-inspired patterned garments, caps and palace details are comparative reconstructions, not exact Susa artifacts.

EST-002.title: Esther’s Banquet
EST-002.q: The adversary and enemy is this wicked Haman.
EST-002.alt: Esther speaks to Ahasuerus at a private banquet as Haman watches uneasily.
EST-002.note: The banquet uses couches and a low table. The speakers can rise from a reclined position; precise caps, fabrics and room details are reconstructed.

JOB-001.title: Job in Humble Reflection
JOB-001.q: I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee.
JOB-001.alt: Job in a worn plain robe sits on dusty ground beneath an immense sky, reflecting humbly without graphic sores.
JOB-001.note: Exact Job site, date and portrait age are not specified.

PRO-001.title: Wisdom More Precious than Treasure
PRO-001.q: She is more precious than rubies
PRO-001.alt: Symbolic scrolls, an olive branch and a clay oil lamp rest beside irregular silver fragments, a plain gold ring and rough-polished colored stones.
PRO-001.note: An undated symbolic assemblage of wisdom and value; exact minerals and metal weights are not certified.

ECC-001.title: A Time for Every Season
ECC-001.q: a time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted
ECC-001.alt: One continuous ancient autumn landscape with adults planting, tending and harvesting in adjacent field areas.
ECC-001.note: A symbolic visualization of seasons in Ecclesiastes 3. Tree species, crop calendar and simple cart are artistic choices.

ISA-002.title: Isaiah in the Temple
ISA-002.q: I saw also the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple.
ISA-002.alt: Isaiah kneels beneath two six-winged seraphim before a high throne concealed by glory, with a woven robe train spread across the steps and floor.
ISA-002.note: Visionary forms, exact wing folding and Temple setting are artistic interpretation, rather than a surveyed room or visible historical portrait.

ISA-001.title: On Eagles' Wings
ISA-001.q: they shall mount up with wings as eagles
ISA-001.alt: A natural golden eagle soars above vast Judean mountain ranges beneath a luminous break in the clouds.

JER-001.title: At the Potter’s House
JER-001.q: as the clay is in the potter’s hand, so are ye in mine hand
JER-001.alt: Jeremiah quietly watches a potter reshape clay on a simple ancient wheel in a humble sunlit workshop.
JER-001.note: Specific wheel, site and town plan are interpreted. Selected instant between marring and remaking follows Jeremiah 18:4.

EZK-001.title: Life Restored in the Valley
EZK-001.q: the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army.
EZK-001.alt: Ezekiel overlooks a broad valley filled with living adults in modest linen, restored hope in morning light.
EZK-001.note: Symbolic restoration of Israel after Ezekiel 37:10–14. This living mixed host represents the restored people, rather than the earlier dry-bone stage or a measured military formation.

DAN-003.title: Daniel Prays at the Window
DAN-003.q: he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God
DAN-003.alt: Daniel prays beside an open upper-room window while two officials watch from the doorway.
DAN-003.note: Daniel prays at an open window. Officials' patterned robes, soft caps and the Babylon panorama are illustrative; compass direction and the actual Jerusalem bearing are not visually certified.

DAN-001.title: Daniel Among the Lions
DAN-001.q: My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions’ mouths
DAN-001.alt: Daniel stands calmly within a stone den while several natural lions rest peacefully at a safe distance.
DAN-001.note: An interior view at the morning rescue in Daniel 6:19–23. The earlier sealed condition has ended; the king is outside this composition.

JON-002.title: Jonah Asleep During the Storm
JON-002.q: Jonah was gone down into the sides of the ship; and he lay, and was fast asleep.
JON-002.alt: A concerned captain wakes Jonah in the ship’s lower hold as a storm rages above.
JON-002.note: Jonah eyes are closed; exact ship fittings are reconstructed. This does not assert every ancient barrel impossible.

JON-001.title: Jonah Returns to Dry Land
JON-001.q: it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land.
JON-001.alt: Jonah sits safely on dry shore in a wet robe while the great fish’s back remains far out at sea.

JON-003.title: Jonah Preaches in Nineveh
JON-003.q: Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown.
JON-003.alt: Jonah preaches to attentive people wearing sackcloth in a street of Nineveh.
JON-003.note: Repentant people at an imagined Nineveh gate. Assyrian-inspired motifs and sackcloth are reconstructed; the exact gate and ancestry of figures are not certified.

MAT-015.title: Joseph’s Dream
MAT-015.q: the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream
MAT-015.alt: Joseph of Nazareth sleeps on a woven mat as a white-robed angel messenger stands near the doorway of a lamplit stone house at night.
MAT-015.note: Joseph’s dream is shown as an artistic visualization; the messenger’s appearance, distant lights and vegetation are not specified as historical portraits or a measured location.

MAT-001.title: The Magi Visit
MAT-001.q: they presented unto him gifts; gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.
MAT-001.alt: Eastern adult travelers present gold, incense and myrrh to a fully clothed young Jesus seated safely on Mary’s lap in a humble house.
MAT-001.note: The visitors' count, ancestry and exact clothing are artistic choices. Matthew describes a house and child without specifying the child’s exact elapsed age; background is not a surveyed Bethlehem view.

MAT-002.title: The Journey to Egypt
MAT-002.q: he took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt
MAT-002.alt: Mary safely cradles warmly wrapped young Jesus on a calm donkey while Joseph walks beside her on a broad level desert path toward dawn.

MAT-003.title: John Beside the Jordan
MAT-003.q: Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
MAT-003.alt: John the Baptist, weathered olive-brown face, coarse dark beard and unkempt dark hair, rough camel-hair garment and leather belt, preaches peacefully to attentive adults beside the Jordan.

MAT-004.title: The Baptism of Jesus
MAT-004.q: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
MAT-004.alt: Jesus, early-thirties Galilean Jewish man, olive-brown skin, dark eyes, shoulder-length dark wavy hair and short full beard, opaque off-white linen and earth-brown mantle, stands beside John during baptism in the shallow Jordan. Natural dove descends; no human God.

MAT-005.title: Jesus in the Wilderness
MAT-005.q: Then was Jesus led up of the Spirit into the wilderness
MAT-005.alt: Jesus with established identity sits alone on a rock in quiet prayer within a vast austere Judean wilderness. Dusty off-white linen and brown mantle, natural dawn light, no halo or cartoon devil.

MAT-006.title: The Sermon on the Mount
MAT-006.q: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
MAT-006.alt: Jesus teaches from a grassy hillside to attentive local families, with the Sea of Galilee beyond.

MAT-007.title: Teaching the Lord’s Prayer
MAT-007.q: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.
MAT-007.alt: An intimate view of Jesus teaching prayer to three listening adult disciples on a Galilean hillside.
MAT-007.note: Distant roofs and vegetation are contextual details; a cypress-like tree alone does not date this scene.

MAT-017.title: The Centurion’s Request
MAT-017.q: speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed.
MAT-017.alt: Jesus listens to a respectful unhelmeted centurion asking for help for his servant.
MAT-017.note: The centurion’s simple clothing is a conservative reconstruction; Matthew 8 does not specify his regiment or ancestry.

MAT-018.title: Peter’s Mother-in-Law Is Restored
MAT-018.q: he touched her hand, and the fever left her
MAT-018.alt: Jesus holds the hand of Peter’s restored mother-in-law as Peter watches gratefully beside her bed.

MAT-016.title: Jesus Calls Matthew
MAT-016.q: he saith unto him, Follow me. And he arose, and followed him.
MAT-016.alt: Jesus invites Matthew to leave his tax booth, where coins and a closed account roll rest on a low desk.
MAT-016.note: The collector’s booth, working table and coin denominations are reconstructed; the table is not a dining arrangement.

MAT-019.title: The Mustard Seed and the Tree
MAT-019.q: the birds of the air come and lodge in the branches thereof.
MAT-019.alt: Small birds shelter in a large flowering mustard plant above a Galilean garden.
MAT-019.note: A selected mustard-type visualization of the parable; the text does not uniquely establish its botanical species or a photographic seed scale.

MAT-020.title: The Pearl of Great Value
MAT-020.q: Who, when he had found one pearl of great price, went and sold all that he had, and bought it.
MAT-020.alt: A merchant admires a single pearl above dark cloth on his market table.
MAT-020.note: The prop was conservatively omitted; this is not a categorical dating claim for all ancient balances.

MAT-008.title: Jesus Walks on the Water
MAT-008.q: Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.
MAT-008.alt: Jesus approaches a wooden boat across rough lake water in dark predawn light; Peter remains inside at the selected moment before stepping out.
MAT-008.note: Selected moment Matthew 14:24-27, before Peter steps out of the boat.

MAT-021.title: Peter’s Confession
MAT-021.q: Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.
MAT-021.alt: Peter speaks to Jesus beside a stream near Caesarea Philippi.

MAT-009.title: The Transfiguration
MAT-009.q: his face did shine as the sun, and his raiment was white as the light.
MAT-009.alt: Jesus shines in white linen between Moses and Elijah on a rocky mountain while three adult disciples watch.

MAT-010.title: The Entry into Jerusalem
MAT-010.q: Hosanna to the Son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord
MAT-010.alt: Jesus rides a donkey toward Jerusalem as a joyful crowd lays cloaks and palm branches along the road.
MAT-010.note: Matthew 21 includes the ass and colt. Riding the colt with the mother accompanying is the selected narrative visualization.

MAT-011.title: The Temple Courtyard
MAT-011.q: overthrew the tables of the moneychangers, and the seats of them that sold doves
MAT-011.alt: Jesus stands firmly beside overturned money tables and scattered coins in the Temple court, with adults stepping back.
MAT-011.note: A selected aftermath of the cleansing. The Temple facade and complete court layout are interpretive, not measured reconstructions.

MAT-012.title: Prayer in Gethsemane
MAT-012.q: O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me
MAT-012.alt: Jesus kneels among old olive trees in Gethsemane at night while three adult disciples sleep at a distance.
MAT-012.note: Selected prayer span rather than the precise face-on-ground instant of Matthew 26:39. Downcast irises and sleeping disciples' fine faces are not assessable.

MAT-013.title: Torches in the Garden
MAT-013.alt: Jesus stands calmly among olive trees as torchbearers approach and Judas stands nearby, with no active violence.

MAT-022.title: The Women Meet the Risen Jesus
MAT-022.q: they came and held him by the feet, and worshipped him.
MAT-022.alt: Mary Magdalene and the other Mary kneel gratefully beside the risen Jesus on a dawn path.

MAT-014.title: The Great Commission
MAT-014.q: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations
MAT-014.alt: Jesus speaks to exactly eleven adult disciples on a hopeful Galilean mountainside beside the lake.

MRK-010.title: Jesus Restores the Man Who Kneels
MRK-010.q: put forth his hand, and touched him, and saith unto him, I will; be thou clean.
MRK-010.alt: Jesus touches the shoulder of a grateful man kneeling outside a village after restoration.
MRK-010.note: Shows the healed man’s joyful response; low plain background buildings are contextual, not a site reconstruction.

MRK-001.title: The Paralytic Is Restored
MRK-001.q: And immediately he arose, took up the bed, and went forth before them all
MRK-001.alt: A restored adult man rises with his rolled bedmat beside Jesus in a crowded Capernaum room, roof opening above.

MRK-006.title: The Sower Goes Out
MRK-006.q: Behold, there went out a sower to sow
MRK-006.alt: A farmer scatters grain across a field beside a path, rocks and thorny ground.

MRK-002.title: Peace over the Storm
MRK-002.q: Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
MRK-002.alt: Jesus stands calmly with his disciples in a wooden boat as lake water settles and storm clouds retreat.
MRK-002.note: Mark 4:35 begins in the evening; exact crossing duration is not asserted. Fine irises and full disciple attendance are outside what this view certifies.

MRK-003.title: Jairus’s Daughter Restored
MRK-003.q: he took the damsel by the hand, and said unto her, Talitha cumi
MRK-003.alt: Jesus holds the hand of Jairus daughter as she sits upright with her parents beside her. Peter, James and John watch from the doorway.
MRK-003.note: Doorway faces and downcast Jesus irises have visibility limits. The wider frame makes the named attendance explicit without claiming the old close crop proved their absence.

MRK-009.title: Jesus at the Carpenter’s Bench
MRK-009.q: Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary
MRK-009.alt: In an interpretive biographical scene, adult Jesus smooths timber at a carpenter’s bench in Nazareth.
MRK-009.note: Interpretive biographical scene: Mark 6:3 calls Jesus a carpenter but does not narrate this particular workshop event; setting and activity are reconstructed.

MRK-011.title: The Man Hears and Speaks
MRK-011.q: straightway his ears were opened, and the string of his tongue was loosed, and he spake plain.
MRK-011.alt: A restored man hears birds and speaks joyfully beside Jesus, with companions at a distance.
MRK-011.note: Shows the man’s joy after hearing is restored, apart from distant bystanders. His eye color and ancestry are not specified by the passage.

MRK-004.title: Jesus Welcomes the Children
MRK-004.q: Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not
MRK-004.alt: Jesus sits warmly greeting modestly clothed children while parents stand nearby in a safe village courtyard.

MRK-007.title: The Rich Young Man’s Question
MRK-007.q: Good Master, what shall I do that I may inherit eternal life?
MRK-007.alt: A richly dressed young man kneels before Jesus on a village road.
MRK-007.note: Shows the questioner before his sorrowful departure; background trees and buildings are contextual, not a precise location.

MRK-012.title: Bartimaeus Answers the Call
MRK-012.q: And he, casting away his garment, rose, and came to Jesus.
MRK-012.alt: Bartimaeus rises beside the Jericho road and turns gratefully toward Jesus, his cloak left behind.
MRK-012.note: This selects Mark 10:52 after Bartimaeus receives sight.

MRK-008.title: The Withered Fig Tree
MRK-008.q: Master, behold, the fig tree which thou cursedst is withered away.
MRK-008.alt: Peter points toward a withered fig tree as Jesus speaks about faith and prayer.

MRK-005.title: The Widow’s Offering
MRK-005.q: she threw in two mites, which make a farthing.
MRK-005.alt: A poor widow drops two small coins into the temple treasury as Jesus watches.
MRK-005.note: Generic treasury receptacle is a contextual interpretation, not a measured Temple collection box. Fine iris detail is limited.

LUK-001.title: The Annunciation
LUK-001.q: Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word.
LUK-001.alt: Young adult Jewish Mary with olive-brown oval face, dark eyes, cream head covering and blue-gray mantle listens in wonder to Gabriel, a dignified white-robed messenger, in a modest stone Nazareth courtyard. Soft natural light, no halos.
LUK-001.note: Courtyard and village are contextual reconstructions; the shrub is not identified as a particular species.

LUK-002.title: Mary Visits Elizabeth
LUK-002.q: Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb.
LUK-002.alt: Same young adult Mary warmly embraces elderly Elizabeth in a humble Judean village doorway. Modest robes, affectionate joyful faces.
LUK-002.note: Elizabeth’s pregnancy is suggested under draped clothing; exact appearance and village setting are interpretive.

LUK-003.title: The Nativity
LUK-003.q: wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger
LUK-003.alt: Same Mary and bearded adult Joseph in earth-brown robe and tan headscarf lovingly watch securely swaddled newborn Jesus lying safely in a straw-lined manger. Rough stone shelter and warm oil lamp; no Magi.
LUK-003.note: Manger material, shelter layout and distant lamplight are artistic reconstructions.

LUK-004.title: The Shepherds Visit
LUK-004.q: found Mary, and Joseph, and the babe lying in a manger.
LUK-004.alt: Modestly dressed adult shepherds visit the established Holy Family and securely swaddled infant manger in a humble stone shelter. Natural sheep behind, quiet joyful night, no Magi or royal gifts.
LUK-004.note: Shepherd count, sheep breed and shelter setting are interpretive.

LUK-017.title: The Angel and the Shepherds
LUK-017.q: Fear not: for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy
LUK-017.alt: Shepherds and sheep watch a radiant white-robed angel on a Judean hillside beneath stars and a distant heavenly host.
LUK-017.note: The host is a visionary visualization; sheep breed, host count and distant lighting are unspecified.

LUK-005.title: Jesus Presented at the Temple
LUK-005.q: Then took he him up in his arms, and blessed God
LUK-005.alt: Elderly Simeon securely cradles the swaddled infant with head supported and face uncovered while established Mary, Joseph and elderly Anna look on gratefully in the Jerusalem temple courtyard.
LUK-005.note: Bird species and measured Temple layout are not certified. Offering is contextual rather than a required simultaneous hand position during Simeon speech.

LUK-018.title: The Family Returns to Nazareth
LUK-018.q: they returned into Galilee, to their own city Nazareth.
LUK-018.alt: Mary carries infant Jesus beside Joseph as the family returns to modest Nazareth houses after the purification.
LUK-018.note: This selects Luke 2:39’s transition after purification, with Jesus as an infant. Exact elapsed age and harmonization with Matthew are not established by the image.

LUK-006.title: Jesus Among the Teachers
LUK-006.q: sitting in the midst of the doctors, both hearing them, and asking them questions.
LUK-006.alt: Twelve-year-old Jesus, clean-faced and fully clothed with youthful proportions, sits safely among adult teachers discussing scrolls in the temple court. Mary and Joseph arrive relieved, naturally aged twelve years.
LUK-006.note: Scroll writing and complete Temple court layout are unassessable. Ancient rollers are not categorically prohibited.

LUK-019.title: Jesus Reads in Nazareth
LUK-019.q: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me
LUK-019.alt: Jesus reads an opened scroll at a simple desk in a stone Nazareth synagogue while adults listen.
LUK-019.note: The assembly room and scroll completion are reconstructed. Ornate finials were simplified; this does not assert that all ancient wooden scroll rollers were impossible.

LUK-007.title: The Fishermen Are Called
LUK-007.q: Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord.
LUK-007.alt: Peter kneels at Jesus knees inside one of two fish-laden boats. James and John lift nets in the other boat, with water visible between the hulls.
LUK-007.note: Exact catch quantity, distant town and fine background facial details are not certified. James is a newly established artistic actor based on the original rear-left fisherman.

LUK-020.title: The Fishermen Leave Their Nets
LUK-020.q: they forsook all, and followed him.
LUK-020.alt: James, Peter and John walk after Jesus along the shore, leaving two boats and nets behind.
LUK-020.note: James and John reuse LUK-007 designs; exact portrait ages and full lakeside site are not certified. The earlier two-person crop did not establish absence from the event.

LUK-022.title: The Crowd Seeks Healing
LUK-022.q: the whole multitude sought to touch him
LUK-022.alt: Jesus holds a seated elder’s hand while families wait on level Galilean ground.
LUK-022.note: A close encounter represents part of the gathering on the plain; full crowd and precise site are outside the frame.

LUK-028.title: The Widow of Nain Receives Her Son
LUK-028.q: And he that was dead sat up, and began to speak. And he delivered him to his mother.
LUK-028.alt: Jesus presents the living young man to his relieved mother beside a stopped bier outside Nain.
LUK-028.note: Shows reunion after the young man sits up. The gate is contextual, rather than an excavated Nain reconstruction.

LUK-029.title: Forgiveness at Simon’s Table
LUK-029.q: Thy faith hath saved thee; go in peace.
LUK-029.alt: At Simon’s meal Jesus turns compassionately toward an unnamed woman with an alabaster vessel near his feet.
LUK-029.note: Luke 7’s woman is unnamed here; she is not identified as either Mary.

LUK-024.title: Jesus Sends the Messengers
LUK-024.q: sent them two and two before his face into every city and place
LUK-024.alt: Jesus sends messengers out in pairs along a path toward nearby villages.
LUK-024.note: A few pairs represent the larger mission; buildings and route are contextual.

LUK-008.title: The Good Samaritan
LUK-008.q: bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine, and set him on his own beast
LUK-008.alt: A Samaritan steadies a bandaged adult traveler safely seated on a donkey along a stony road, offering care.
LUK-008.note: An illustrative parable location, not a recovered road site or an ancestry claim.

LUK-011.title: Mary and Martha
LUK-011.q: which also sat at Jesus’ feet, and heard his word
LUK-011.alt: Jesus teaches in a modest Bethany home while Mary listens near his feet and Martha holds a bread tray.
LUK-011.note: Dates and olives are a conservative prop choice; the edit does not establish that apples were impossible in the ancient Mediterranean.

LUK-023.title: The Lost Coin Is Found
LUK-023.q: Rejoice with me; for I have found the piece which I had lost.
LUK-023.alt: A woman holds up a found silver coin as her neighbors rejoice at the doorway.

LUK-009.title: The Prodigal Son Returns
LUK-009.q: his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
LUK-009.alt: An elderly father warmly embraces his adult younger son in dusty robes outside the family home.
LUK-009.note: The father welcomes his son before the feast; estate and flock are contextual parable details.

LUK-021.title: The Grateful Samaritan Returns
LUK-021.q: fell down on his face at his feet, giving him thanks
LUK-021.alt: A grateful Samaritan kneels before Jesus on a village path.
LUK-021.note: Shows the thankful return and conversation; others are outside this scene and the village is unidentified.

LUK-012.title: Zacchaeus in the Sycamore
LUK-012.q: climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him
LUK-012.alt: Zacchaeus sits securely on a broad low sycamore branch, looking toward Jesus and a crowd below in Jericho.
LUK-012.note: The selected tree model follows sycomore-fig morphology. Synthetic leaves do not certify a particular specimen, and Zacchaeus’s stature cannot be measured while seated.

LUK-025.title: Jesus Looks Over Jerusalem
LUK-025.q: he beheld the city, and wept over it
LUK-025.alt: Jesus weeps as he looks over Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives.
LUK-025.note: Intentionally simplified hazy skyline, not a complete measured AD 30 Jerusalem reconstruction. Oblique wet iris hue unassessable.

LUK-013.title: The Last Supper
LUK-013.q: he took bread, and gave thanks, and brake it
LUK-013.alt: Jesus gives thanks over bread and wine at a low table with exactly twelve apostles, thirteen men in the upper room.

LUK-014.title: Peter in the Courtyard
LUK-014.q: while he yet spake, the cock crew.
LUK-014.alt: Peter sits troubled beside a charcoal fire in a stone courtyard, with a rooster on the wall and dawn approaching.
LUK-014.note: Shows Peter’s troubled pause by the fire; courtyard fixtures and skyline are contextual, rather than a measured residence.

LUK-030.title: Jesus Before the Council
LUK-030.q: Art thou then the Son of God? And he said unto them, Ye say that I am.
LUK-030.alt: Jesus stands with dignity before seated council elders in a Jerusalem stone chamber at dawn.

LUK-031.title: Simon Carries the Cross
LUK-031.q: on him they laid the cross, that he might bear it after Jesus.
LUK-031.alt: Jesus walks ahead as Simon of Cyrene carries a rough crossbeam through a Jerusalem street.
LUK-031.note: A close view of Simon carrying the crossbeam after Jesus. Escorts are outside the frame and skyline is contextual.

LUK-015.title: The Crucifixion
LUK-015.q: there was a darkness over all the earth until the ninth hour.
LUK-015.alt: Three distant crosses stand on a rocky hill beneath a darkened sky, with fully clothed adult witnesses nearby.

LUK-026.title: The Women at the Empty Tomb
LUK-026.q: Why seek ye the living among the dead?
LUK-026.alt: Mary Magdalene and two women meet two white-robed messengers at the empty tomb at dawn.
LUK-026.note: Bowed full faces and irises unassessable. Three visible women are a selected group, not a full attendance count. Round stone and rich tomb form are interpretive, not an identified historical tomb.

LUK-016.title: The Road to Emmaus
LUK-016.q: Jesus himself drew near, and went with them.
LUK-016.alt: Jesus walks beside exactly two adult disciples through the Judean hills in late-afternoon conversation.
LUK-016.note: Evening road conversation in Luke 24:13–29; no exact archaeological Emmaus location is asserted.

LUK-032.title: Recognized in the Breaking of Bread
LUK-032.q: their eyes were opened, and they knew him
LUK-032.alt: Jesus breaks bread at Emmaus as the same two travelers from the road recognize him.
LUK-032.note: Luke 24:30–32 names bread without specifying its thickness; this view does not certify visible wounds.

LUK-027.title: Peace Among the Disciples
LUK-027.q: Jesus himself stood in the midst of them, and saith unto them, Peace be unto you.
LUK-027.alt: The risen Jesus speaks peace to joyful Peter, John and other disciples in a lamplit room.

JHN-021.title: Andrew Brings Simon to Jesus
JHN-021.q: And he brought him to Jesus.
JHN-021.alt: Andrew introduces Simon to Jesus on a quiet path near the Jordan.
JHN-021.note: John 1:40–42: Andrew brings Simon to Jesus. Village, precise location, trees and dress are artistic reconstruction; these verses do not identify this exact site.

JHN-014.title: Philip Brings Nathanael
JHN-014.q: Philip saith unto him, Come and see.
JHN-014.alt: Philip introduces Nathanael to Jesus on a Galilean path near a fig tree.

JHN-001.title: The Wedding at Cana
JHN-001.q: there was a marriage in Cana of Galilee
JHN-001.alt: Jesus attends a joyful village wedding beside exactly six large stone water jars, with servants and adult guests.
JHN-001.note: Large lathe-turned chalkstone vessel comparisons inform the selected forms; these are not recovered Cana vessels or a certified two/three-firkin volume.

JHN-022.title: The Servants Fill Six Stone Jars
JHN-022.q: Fill the waterpots with water. And they filled them up to the brim.
JHN-022.alt: Servants pour clear water into six stone jars while Jesus gives an instruction in the Cana courtyard.
JHN-022.note: Six servants are an artistic grouping, not a number supplied by John 2. The comparative jars are not recovered Cana artifacts or certified capacities.

JHN-002.title: Nicodemus Visits at Night
JHN-002.q: The same came to Jesus by night
JHN-002.alt: Jesus and older Nicodemus speak thoughtfully on a quiet lamplit stone terrace at night.
JHN-002.note: Moon and room are selected night cues; no precise dated phase or archaeological conversation site is asserted.

JHN-003.title: The Woman at the Well
JHN-003.q: There cometh a woman of Samaria to draw water: Jesus saith unto her, Give me to drink.
JHN-003.alt: Jesus sits beside a stone well speaking respectfully with a Samaritan woman holding a clay water jar at midday.
JHN-003.note: Jesus speaks with an unnamed Samaritan woman. Well equipment and village are reconstructed; the view does not establish Mount Gerizim’s exact orientation.

JHN-015.title: The Man at Bethesda Walks
JHN-015.q: the man was made whole, and took up his bed, and walked
JHN-015.alt: The restored man carries his rolled mat beside the Bethesda pool and looks toward Jesus.
JHN-015.note: The restored man takes up his bed and walks. Pool, colonnade and skyline are reconstructed; the partial view does not document all five porches.

JHN-004.title: Feeding the Five Thousand
JHN-004.q: Jesus took the loaves; and when he had given thanks, he distributed to the disciples
JHN-004.alt: Jesus gives thanks over exactly five barley loaves and two fish while disciples distribute food to seated families.
JHN-004.note: John 6:9,11 specifies five barley loaves and two small fish. Grain composition, centimetre size, fine irises and complete crowd count are not visually certified; no unleavened-bread requirement is asserted.

JHN-016.title: The Man Washes at Siloam
JHN-016.q: He went his way therefore, and washed, and came seeing.
JHN-016.alt: A man kneels on a broad step and washes his eyes with water from the pool of Siloam.

JHN-005.title: The Good Shepherd
JHN-005.q: he goeth before them, and the sheep follow him: for they know his voice.
JHN-005.alt: Jesus gently guides a flock through a simple wooden gate in a stone sheepfold in natural daylight.
JHN-005.note: A symbolic Good Shepherd illustration of John 10:1–18. Sheepfold, gate and fleece are reconstructed, rather than a documented literal visit described by the discourse.

JHN-024.title: Martha Meets Jesus Outside Bethany
JHN-024.q: I am the resurrection, and the life
JHN-024.alt: Martha meets Jesus on the path outside Bethany before Lazarus is raised.

JHN-025.title: Jesus Weeps at Bethany
JHN-025.alt: Jesus weeps quietly while Mary of Bethany kneels grieving before Lazarus is raised.
JHN-025.note: Mary of Bethany has fallen at Jesus’s feet, and he weeps. This depicts the following tearful interval without asserting visible hand-to-foot contact; she is distinct from Magdalene and Jesus’s mother.

JHN-006.title: Lazarus Comes Out
JHN-006.q: And he that was dead came forth, bound hand and foot with graveclothes
JHN-006.alt: Living Lazarus emerges upright from a rock-cut tomb in linen wrappings as Jesus, Mary and Martha watch joyfully.

JHN-007.title: Anointing at Bethany
JHN-007.q: anointed the feet of Jesus, and wiped his feet with her hair
JHN-007.alt: Mary of Bethany reverently anoints Jesus’s feet and wipes them with her hair, with Martha and Lazarus behind.
JHN-007.note: The tight crop shows four core participants; it does not assert that no other dinner guests were present.

JHN-008.title: Jesus Washes the Disciples' Feet
JHN-008.q: Lord, dost thou wash my feet?
JHN-008.alt: Jesus in plain linen and a towel gently washes Peter’s feet in a basin while other disciples watch quietly.

JHN-017.title: The Vine and the Branches
JHN-017.q: I am the vine, ye are the branches
JHN-017.alt: In a symbolic illustration of his teaching, Jesus gestures toward a vine and its connected fruit-bearing branches.

JHN-009.title: Jesus Before Pilate
JHN-009.q: My kingdom is not of this world
JHN-009.alt: Jesus stands uninjured and dignified before Roman governor Pilate in a Jerusalem stone hall during quiet questioning.
JHN-009.note: Pilate’s toga or mantle is a wardrobe interpretation, not a proven impossibility. Guards are outside this tight conversation crop; no unit or ancestry is assigned.

JHN-019.title: The Burial in the Garden Tomb
JHN-019.q: Then took they the body of Jesus, and wound it in linen clothes with the spices
JHN-019.alt: Nicodemus and Joseph of Arimathea lay the fully linen-wrapped body of Jesus on a garden-tomb bench.
JHN-019.note: John 19:38–42: single visible jar does not represent the entire spice supply. Covered Jesus face, precise tomb and garden species are unassessable.

JHN-010.title: The Empty Tomb
JHN-010.q: he stooping down, and looking in, saw the linen clothes lying
JHN-010.alt: Peter and John look into an empty rock-cut tomb with linen wrappings, the round stone rolled aside at dawn.
JHN-010.note: Peter and the other disciple find linen and the separate head cloth. Tomb and skyline are reconstructed; the scene follows Mary’s earlier arrival while it was dark.

JHN-011.title: Mary Magdalene in the Garden
JHN-011.q: Jesus saith unto her, Mary. She turned herself, and saith unto him, Rabboni
JHN-011.alt: Risen Jesus and Mary Magdalene recognize one another in a garden near the tomb at dawn, with gentle joy.
JHN-011.note: The healed palm mark supplies visual continuity with later resurrection scenes; John 20:11-18 does not explicitly narrate a display of wounds.

JHN-012.title: Thomas Meets the Risen Jesus
JHN-012.q: Reach hither thy finger, and behold my hands
JHN-012.alt: Jesus shows his open hands to astonished Thomas in a lamplit room while other disciples watch.

JHN-013.title: Breakfast by the Sea
JHN-013.q: Jesus saith unto them, Come and dine.
JHN-013.alt: Jesus and seven disciples share bread and fish beside a charcoal fire on the shore of Galilee at dawn.
JHN-013.note: Seven disciples meet Jesus beside a coal fire with fish and bread. The rack is a plausible ancient cooking interpretation; John does not specify one, and its exact Galilean form is unverified.

JHN-020.title: Jesus Restores Peter
JHN-020.q: Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me?
JHN-020.alt: Jesus and Peter speak beside a fading breakfast fire on the shore of Galilee.

ACT-001.title: The Ascension
ACT-001.q: he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight.
ACT-001.alt: Jesus rises into a luminous cloud above eleven disciples and two white-robed messengers on the Mount of Olives.
ACT-001.note: Acts 1:9–11 gives the cloud and two men in white. Distant city layout, light and exact appearance of the ascent are artistic reconstruction.

ACT-002.title: The Day of Pentecost
ACT-002.q: there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire
ACT-002.alt: Adult women and men, including Mary, gather in an upper room beneath small harmless flame-like tongues of light.
ACT-002.note: Acts 2 describes a shared house and tongues like fire. Mary’s inclusion draws on Acts 1:14; room and visible gathering are reconstructed without a complete attendance claim.

ACT-003.title: At the Beautiful Gate
ACT-003.q: he took him by the right hand, and lifted him up
ACT-003.alt: Peter and the younger short-curled John help a joyful restored man stand at the Beautiful Gate.
ACT-003.note: Acts 4:22 identifies the man as over forty; numerical age cannot be measured from a face. Gate appearance and location are reconstructed, without a certain Nicanor identification.

ACT-004.title: Philip and the Ethiopian Official
ACT-004.alt: Philip and an Ethiopian official study a scroll together in a stopped ancient chariot beside a desert road.
ACT-004.note: Acts 8 specifies a chariot, Isaiah reading and Philip joining the official. Vehicle, canopy, wheel forms, ornament, dress and scroll fittings are reconstructed.

ACT-005.title: Saul on the Damascus Road
ACT-005.q: suddenly there shined round about him a light from heaven
ACT-005.alt: Saul kneels on the Damascus road under intense radiance, with adult companions standing at a distance.

ACT-011.title: Ananias Visits Saul
ACT-011.q: there fell from his eyes as it had been scales: and he received sight forthwith
ACT-011.alt: Ananias rests his hands on seated Saul’s shoulders in a sunlit Damascus house as Saul looks up with relief.

ACT-021.title: Paul Is Lowered from Damascus
ACT-021.q: let him down by the wall in a basket.
ACT-021.alt: Followers lower Paul safely in a woven basket from a Damascus wall opening at night.
ACT-021.note: Basket underside and exact lamp spout are cropped or occluded. Actual escape-window location is unknown.

ACT-012.title: Barnabas Welcomes Saul
ACT-012.q: But Barnabas took him, and brought him to the apostles
ACT-012.alt: Barnabas warmly welcomes younger Saul in a Jerusalem courtyard as adult believers look on.

ACT-006.title: Peter and Cornelius
ACT-006.q: Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons
ACT-006.alt: Peter and the unarmed Roman Cornelius speak respectfully as equals while adult family members listen.

ACT-020.title: Peter Is Led Out of Prison
ACT-020.q: the iron gate that leadeth unto the city; which opened to them of his own accord
ACT-020.alt: Peter follows an angel through an open prison gate into a moonlit Jerusalem street.
ACT-020.note: Acts 12:10 specifies the iron gate. Prison, street and skyline are reconstructed; messenger appearance is an artistic choice.

ACT-013.title: Paul and Barnabas Are Sent
ACT-013.q: when they had fasted and prayed, and laid their hands on them, they sent them away.
ACT-013.alt: Paul and Barnabas sit in prayer as three leaders lay hands on their shoulders before sending them from Antioch.
ACT-013.note: Acts 13 names Simeon called Niger and Lucius of Cyrene without supplying portraits. Supporting elders are not individually identified; room and travel bundles are reconstructed.

ACT-022.title: The Mission Arrives in Cyprus
ACT-022.q: from thence they sailed to Cyprus.
ACT-022.alt: Paul, Barnabas and young adult John Mark carry tied cloth bundles through the port of Salamis beside a wooden merchant ship and low Roman warehouses.
ACT-022.note: Exact Salamis port plan, John Mark numerical age and ancestry are not established by the text.

ACT-024.title: Paul Speaks in Pisidian Antioch
ACT-024.q: Men of Israel, and ye that fear God, give audience.
ACT-024.alt: Paul addresses listeners in the Pisidian Antioch synagogue while Barnabas sits nearby.
ACT-024.note: Synagogue setting, wood screens, hanging oil lamp and scroll fittings are illustrative; no specific excavated Pisidian synagogue interior is asserted.

ACT-014.title: The Man at Lystra Walks
ACT-014.q: Stand upright on thy feet. And he leaped and walked.
ACT-014.alt: A joyful man takes confident steps in Lystra as Paul encourages him and townspeople watch.
ACT-014.note: Lycaonian crowd garments and appearance are illustrative regional choices. Street and vegetation are reconstructed; the passage does not assign every person a fixed ethnic uniform.

ACT-025.title: Elders Are Appointed in the Churches
ACT-025.q: when they had ordained them elders in every church, and had prayed with fasting
ACT-025.alt: Paul and Barnabas pray with newly appointed elders in a sunny house courtyard.

ACT-026.title: The First Journey Is Reported
ACT-026.q: how he had opened the door of faith unto the Gentiles.
ACT-026.alt: Paul and Barnabas joyfully report their journey to the church in Syrian Antioch.
ACT-026.note: Acts 14:27 describes reporting to the gathered church. Courtyard, bundles, plants and attendance are reconstructed.

ACT-027.title: The Council in Jerusalem
ACT-027.q: Peter rose up, and said unto them, Men and brethren
ACT-027.alt: Peter addresses the Jerusalem council while Paul and Barnabas listen nearby.

ACT-028.title: Paul Meets Timothy
ACT-028.q: a certain disciple was there, named Timotheus
ACT-028.alt: Paul warmly welcomes Timothy outside a home in Lystra, with a travel satchel ready.
ACT-028.note: Lystra buildings, tiles, season and greenery are reconstructed. Timothy is shown as a young adult; Acts 16 gives neither exact age nor precise meeting gesture.

ACT-029.title: The Macedonian Call
ACT-029.q: Come over into Macedonia, and help us.
ACT-029.alt: Paul sits in thought beside a small oil lamp after the Macedonian vision, with a dark quay and sea beyond the shutters.
ACT-029.note: Acts 16:10 response after the vision is selected, so no simultaneous Macedonian visitor is depicted. The house and harbor are imagined.

ACT-030.title: Landing at Neapolis
ACT-030.q: we came with a straight course to Samothracia, and the next day to Neapolis
ACT-030.alt: Paul and Silas step onto the Neapolis quay beside a merchant ship and secured gangplank.
ACT-030.note: Harbor, ship, tiles, green slopes and hillside buildings illustrate Roman Macedonia, rather than a recovered Neapolis plan.

ACT-010.title: Lydia Listens Beside the River
ACT-010.q: a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple
ACT-010.alt: Paul speaks with Lydia and other women beside a river near Philippi, with a basket of purple cloth nearby.
ACT-010.note: Back-facing or cropped faces are unassessable. Purple cloth is a contextual trade prop; exact river location is unknown. Roman bridges are not categorically impossible.

ACT-007.title: Paul and Silas in Prison
ACT-007.q: at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God
ACT-007.alt: Paul and Silas pray and sing in an ancient stone cell with an open door and unfastened shackles.
ACT-007.note: Immediately after doors open and bands are loosed in Acts 16:26. This is not a complete pre-earthquake prison inventory; the jailer’s response is outside the frame.

ACT-015.title: The Jailer and His Household
ACT-015.q: he set meat before them, and rejoiced, believing in God with all his house.
ACT-015.alt: Paul and Silas share bread with the joyful jailer’s family around a lamplit table.
ACT-015.note: The meal selects Acts 16:34 after washing and baptism in verse 33. Household ancestry, precise dress, house and lighting are illustrative.

ACT-031.title: Paul Reasons in Thessalonica
ACT-031.q: three sabbath days reasoned with them out of the scriptures
ACT-031.alt: Paul reasons with Thessalonian listeners while Silas listens and a reader holds a scroll.
ACT-031.note: Devout Greeks and women of Acts 17:4 are artistically represented; ancestry is not certified from faces. Exact synagogue plan, crowd size and seating rules are not asserted.

ACT-032.title: The Bereans Examine the Scriptures
ACT-032.q: searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.
ACT-032.alt: Berean readers examine scrolls while Paul and Silas discuss the Scriptures with them.
ACT-032.note: Study table is not a meal. A distant cypress-like tree is not inherently anachronistic in Macedonia. Script content and fine irises are unassessable.

ACT-008.title: Paul Speaks in Athens
ACT-008.q: For in him we live, and move, and have our being
ACT-008.alt: Paul in a deep-blue mantle addresses Greek listeners on the rocky Areopagus, with Athenian temples beyond.
ACT-008.note: An illustrative Athenian setting. Exact Areopagus viewpoint, distance, planting and audience appearance are reconstructed, rather than a surveyed panorama.

ACT-016.title: Paul Works with Priscilla and Aquila
ACT-016.q: by their occupation they were tentmakers.
ACT-016.alt: Paul, Priscilla and Aquila work together sewing tent fabric in a Corinthian workshop.
ACT-016.note: Acts 18 identifies shared tentmaking; materials, loops, needles and workshop are illustrative rather than excavated fittings.

ACT-033.title: Paul Is Encouraged in Corinth
ACT-033.q: Be not afraid, but speak, and hold not thy peace
ACT-033.alt: Paul sits in quiet renewed resolve in a Corinthian home-workshop at night.
ACT-033.note: Acts 18:9 night vision. Room, light and distant houses are reconstructed; no visible divine human figure is asserted.

ACT-034.title: Priscilla and Aquila Teach Apollos
ACT-034.q: expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly.
ACT-034.alt: Priscilla and Aquila explain the way more fully to Apollos in an Ephesian home.
ACT-034.note: Acts 18:26 private explanation to Apollos. Courtyard, furnishings, scroll fittings and distant buildings are illustrative, rather than an identified excavated house.

ACT-017.title: Paul Teaches in Ephesus
ACT-017.q: disputing daily in the school of one Tyrannus.
ACT-017.alt: Paul teaches a seated group of adults in a sunlit Ephesian hall.
ACT-017.note: School setting, scroll fittings, garments and planting are reconstructed. Ordinary woven stripes do not identify a later ritual garment.

ACT-036.title: Eutychus Is Comforted at Troas
ACT-036.q: Trouble not yourselves; for his life is in him.
ACT-036.alt: Paul comforts the awake Eutychus beside relieved adults in a lamplit upper room at Troas.

ACT-035.title: Farewell to the Ephesian Elders
ACT-035.q: he kneeled down, and prayed with them all.
ACT-035.alt: Paul kneels in farewell prayer with the Ephesian elders beside a ship at Miletus.
ACT-035.note: Farewell at Miletus. Harbor, sunset, bundle and partial ship are reconstructed; complete rig is outside the frame and no diagnostic galleon rig is certified.

ACT-037.title: Prayer on the Beach at Tyre
ACT-037.q: we kneeled down on the shore, and prayed.
ACT-037.alt: Paul kneels with believers and their families in farewell prayer on the beach at Tyre.
ACT-037.note: Acts 21:4–6 shore farewell with wives and children. Skyline, vessel and shoreline are reconstructed; exact tower form and plant species are unverified.

ACT-018.title: Paul Before Agrippa
ACT-018.q: Then Paul stretched forth the hand, and answered for himself
ACT-018.alt: Paul speaks with a chain at his wrist before seated Agrippa, Bernice and Festus in a provincial audience hall.
ACT-018.note: Acts 25:23 supplies Agrippa, Bernice and Festus for the hearing; Acts 26 supplies Paul’s speech and reference to his bonds. The hall and the two newly established actor designs are artistic interpretations.

ACT-038.title: Paul Sails Toward Rome
ACT-038.q: And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, we launched
ACT-038.alt: Older Paul boards the Adramyttian merchant vessel under a Roman officer’s supervision.
ACT-038.note: Acts 27:1–2 initial Adramyttian ship is selected, rather than the later Alexandrian ship. Officer equipment, exact restraint construction, harbor and vessel are reconstructed.

ACT-039.title: Paul Breaks Bread During the Storm
ACT-039.q: he took bread, and gave thanks to God in presence of them all
ACT-039.alt: Older Paul gives thanks and breaks bread before sailors and passengers on the storm-worn ship.

ACT-009.title: Safe on the Shore
ACT-009.q: they escaped all safe to land.
ACT-009.alt: Older Paul and other adults gather safely on Malta’s shore, with a broken empty merchant ship offshore.

ACT-040.title: Believers Meet Paul on the Appian Way
ACT-040.q: whom when Paul saw, he thanked God, and took courage.
ACT-040.alt: Roman believers warmly welcome older Paul on the Appian Way near the Market of Appius.

ACT-019.title: Paul Welcomes Visitors in Rome
ACT-019.q: Paul dwelt two whole years in his own hired house, and received all that came in unto him
ACT-019.alt: Older Paul welcomes visitors into his rented Roman house while a guard stands quietly behind him.
ACT-019.note: Some chain is occluded by arm and mantle. Restraint construction, room and visitors are reconstructed; visitor leather flap/loop has no diagnostic modern hardware.

1CO-001.title: The Way of Love
1CO-001.q: Charity suffereth long, and is kind
1CO-001.alt: Two adults offer bread and water to an elderly neighbor at a shared ancient table, illustrating patient love.

EPH-001.title: The Armor of God
EPH-001.q: Put on the whole armour of God
EPH-001.alt: A symbolic adult figure in Roman-inspired armor stands resolutely with a resting shield and a sheathed sword.
EPH-001.note: Ephesians 6:10–18 is a spiritual metaphor. Roman-inspired equipment and landscape are artistic interpretation, not a certified uniform or narrated military event.

REV-001.title: The New Jerusalem
REV-001.q: the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven
REV-001.alt: A transparent golden city shaped as a cube descends above a landscape. Three pearl gates with angels are visible on each of two faces; colored foundation courses run along the base.
REV-001.note: Revelation 21 is a vision. Equal length, breadth and height are interpreted as a cube; only two faces and six of the twelve gates are visible. Exact scale, hidden gates and all foundation courses cannot be verified in this perspective.

REV-002.title: The River and the Tree of Life
REV-002.q: a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal
REV-002.alt: A crystal-clear river flows through a radiant city beside the fruit-bearing Tree of Life and lush green leaves.
REV-002.note: Tree form across both banks and fruit forms visualize symbolic Revelation 22. The picture cannot demonstrate twelve monthly crops; surrounding arches do not identify a separate temple.
